prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: offshore wind farm commissioning/acceptance, operation/maintenance, refurbishment, decommissioning; reliable generation, personnel safety, asset integrity. Boundary: offshore equipment, operational services, shore decision functions with defined interfaces; excludes public-grid assets beyond agreed connection and unrelated port operations.

Aliases: Glassfin = Turbine Controller; Morrowick = Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern = Weather Service; Juniper Vale = SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown = Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay = Shore Control Room.

Elements: Turbine Controller controls individual turbines locally and produces Pitch Deviation Notice for operational handling; recipient unspecified. Turbine subsystems: Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit; equipment: Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone assesses blades. Offshore Substation collects/switches electricity; contains Main Transformer. Export Cable Monitor monitors export system; Grid Interface Relay interfaces external grid.

SCADA Gateway mediates controlled offshore–shore supervisory exchanges and consistent information access. SCADA Engineer maintains supervisory-interface configuration/integrity. Shore Control Room continuously monitors and coordinates operations/dispatch, sharing operational context. Control Engineer assesses equipment/responds using shore operational picture. Maintenance Planning Engine organizes needs/resources/constraints; Duty Planner prepares/reviews maintenance, retaining judgment. Weather Service supplies environmental information; Metocean Buoy supplies offshore observations. Marine Coordinator considers conditions/vessel availability; Fleet Dispatch Console provides dispatch overview.

Marine/access: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck supports helicopter access; North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner; Personnel Tracking Console locates/accounts for personnel. Warehouse System, Spares Hub support materials logistics. Work Permit Portal supports controlled work authorization; Cybersecurity Gateway supports security. External/enabling: grid dispatch, port support, emergency response organizations, communications, fire protection, backup power. No modes specified.

Requirements: authorize work/control hazards/account personnel/vessels; prevent pollution/minimize disturbance/respond promptly to environmental incidents. Ensure monitoring, timely fault response, planned maintenance/coordinated access. Commissioning requires documented handover/verification. Decisions require validated status, approved procedures/current forecasts/grid instructions. Maintenance considers condition/resources/access/production; unplanned work requires severity-proportional prioritization/controlled mobilization. Decommissioning requires safe isolation/removal planning/residual-record transfer.

New part:
S071: The Cybersecurity Gateway provides a security boundary for connected operational services.
S072: The architecture assigns defined responsibilities to interfaces so that system changes can be assessed and managed.
S073: Operational personnel retain authority for decisions that require procedural, safety, or engineering judgment.
S074: This arrangement supports maintainable operations while keeping supervisory functions distinct from planning and human coordination.
S075: The operating organization combines shore-based planning, marine coordination, vessel crews, and technicians assigned to offshore work.
S076: The Duty Planner develops daily work priorities with input from the Field Supervisor and the Maintenance Planning Engine.
S077: The Marine Coordinator aligns vessel availability with crew readiness, port access, and the planned work locations.
S078: The Crew Transfer Vessel is identified in local procedures by the alias Kestrel Bay.
S079: The Vessel Master retains authority for navigation, vessel safety, and decisions about whether a transfer can proceed.
S080: The Fleet Dispatch Console is identified in local procedures by the alias Sable Orchard.
S081: The Fleet Dispatch Console gives the Marine Coordinator a shared view of vessel assignments, planned movements, and dispatch status.
S082: The Marine Coordinator uses that view to coordinate the Crew Transfer Vessel, the Service Operations Vessel, and the Daughter Craft as conditions require.
S083: The Weather Service produces the Squall Window Bulletin for operational awareness.
S084: The Weather Analyst reviews available forecasts and advises the Marine Coordinator on conditions that may affect marine operations.
S085: The Vessel Master evaluates local conditions before departure and continues to reassess them during the voyage.
S086: A Weather Hold pauses affected marine activity until the responsible personnel confirm that operations can resume safely.
S087: The Crew Transfer Vessel transports authorized personnel and routine tools between shore and offshore work locations.
S088: The Daughter Craft can support short-range transfers when the operating plan and conditions permit its use.
S089: The Service Operations Vessel provides a platform for work that needs longer offshore presence or broader onboard support.
S090: The Warehouse System is identified in local procedures by the alias Mosslight.
S091: The Warehouse System records stock status and supports preparation of equipment and consumables for scheduled work.
S092: The Storekeeper checks requested materials against available stock and coordinates replenishment with the Spares Hub.
S093: The Port Agent supports shore-side arrangements for vessel calls, crew access, and staged cargo.
S094: The Personnel Tracking Console helps the organization maintain an accurate view of personnel assigned to offshore activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
